translation_notes: the mechanical draft only covered the two .add() runs (g{ } + Python +=); this batch redid them as `+{ }` proper -- `@graph g` declared once, right after `g = graph.get_context(graphuri)`, covers every island that targets `g` (2 add sites folded to 1, 3 reads, 1 remove) with no receiver of its own; `g2` is a second, distinct graph live in the SAME function, so its 2 touches use the explicit call suffix `(g2)` instead -- `@graph` names ONE current graph per declaration, and this region genuinely has two.

every OTHER rdflib idiom the region contains was translated too, not only the 'remove' one the stratum sampled -- precedent: ArangoRDB.__add_adb_col_statement and OntologyDeprecator.deprecate elsewhere in this same batch do the same (translate every applicable island, credit each construction separately, regardless of which stratum picked the region). `g.query(LITERAL)` -> `s{ LITERAL }` (sparql_literal, this region's OTHER listed stratum); `g.query(LITERAL, initBindings={'s': tarek})` -> `s{ LITERAL }(bindings={'s': tarek})` -- ?s IS projected (SELECT *) so INSTRUCTIONS SS2's rule applies ('sinon s{ }(bindings=...)', not a bare interpolation); `g.triples(pattern)` (three call sites, two with a wildcard subject/none, one fully bound) -> `m{ pattern }`, kept inside the SAME `len(list(r)) == N` shape the original asserts, not rewritten to bool()/.count() -- no restructuring.

g.remove((tarek, likes, pizza)) -> -{ {tarek} {likes} {pizza} }, the remove stratum's own idiom: no wildcard is present (unlike the sibling YurtleStore.remove/ArangoRDB regions in this batch), so this is the direct, undegraded form.

NOT a hollow green: every read this region performs is guarded by the ORIGINAL's own `assert len(list(r)) == N`, which run_pair's fo(*args)/ft(*args) call executes for real -- a wrong m{ }/s{ } translation raises AssertionError inside the entry point itself, which run_pair reports as an error (checked: narrowing `m{ ?s {likes} {pizza} }` to `m{ ?s {likes} {cheese} }` makes the SECOND assert in the region fail with exactly that traceback). Only the graph's FINAL state additionally needs the Dataset-argument comparison (see driver.py) because the very last line, `r = s{ ... }` after the remove, has no trailing assert in the real upstream test either (confirmed against the fetched source at the pinned commit: the function genuinely ends there) -- so that one line is translated for consistency with the rest but is, like in the source, unverified either way.

verified the remove specifically is not a hollow green: widening it to `-{ ?anything {likes} {pizza} }` (subject wildcard) makes the driver FAIL on `call[0].arg[0]` (the two Datasets no longer isomorphic) -- because at that point in the run `g` holds BOTH tarek-likes-pizza and bob-likes-pizza, so a subject-wildcard removal deletes one triple too many where the fully-bound form deletes exactly one. Restored before finalising.

the real `getgraph` pytest fixture is `ConjunctiveGraph(store='LevelDB')`, an external C-extension store out of reach; the region's own body only ever calls get_context/.add/.remove/.query/.triples, all of which an in-memory `rdflib.Dataset` supports identically, so the driver substitutes one -- see driver.py for why it goes through a `_DatasetProxy` (a pre-existing rdflib/rdfeval interaction: `to_isomorphic` -- what run_pair's generic argument comparison uses for a bare Graph -- raises on a quad-yielding Dataset; same sidestep as the sibling region testUpdateWithInitNs/driver.py, which hits the identical issue from the same source file).

fixture.ttl seeds unrelated data in the DEFAULT graph only, to prove get_context() isolation; the region's own asserted counts (3, 1, 2, 2, 1, 1, 0 triples/solutions at each step) already are the several-solutions / zero-solution / non-matching-neighbour cases the reading oracle asks for, so the fixture does not need to duplicate them -- see its own header.

article_candidate: the -{ } line by itself is unremarkable (one-for-one with g.remove), but the region as a whole -- two graphs, a literal query, initBindings, three .triples() patterns and a remove, ALL translated, ALL still checked by the source test's own asserts -- is a compact demonstration that `m{ }`/`s{ }`/`+{ }`/`-{ }` interoperate under a shared `@graph` without the reads and writes needing to agree on which island form to use.

Reviewed 2026-11-02 (PI decision: m{ } for any BGP in the initBindings queries). The call `g.query("SELECT * WHERE { ?s <urn:likes> <urn:pizza> . }", initBindings={"s": tarek})` is a single triple pattern whose result the test only counts, so it is now `m{ {tarek} <urn:likes> <urn:pizza> }` (a fully bound pattern yields one empty solution per match, so len(list(r)) == 1 as before); the s{ } bindings call suffix is gone. The two other s{ } queries (first, and the lazy one after the removal) carry no initBindings: they are the sparql_literal part of this region (a store test of its SPARQL path) and stay s{ }.

optimization_notes: optimized.py: `graph = getgraph` dropped (get_context called on the parameter); the `r = g.triples(...)` + `assert len(list(r)) == N` pairs inlined, and the two fully bound ones become `assert (tarek, likes, pizza) in g` / `not in g` (a fully bound pattern matches 0 or 1 triple, and __contains__ reads the same store's triples()); the two query results use `len(r)` (rdflib's Result has __len__); the dead `r =` of the last query dropped, the query itself kept. The three adds stay `.add`: this is a store test, and `g +=` would route through addN, another store path.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: `@graph g`; the three adds become one `+{ {tarek} {likes} {pizza} . {bob} {likes} {pizza}, {cheese} }` (object list, island only); the triples-pattern count becomes `m{ ?s {likes} {pizza} }.count()`, the membership tests `assert m{ … }` / `assert not m{ … }`; the initBindings query (a one-pattern BGP, PI decision) becomes `assert m{ {tarek} {likes} {pizza} }.count() == 1`, on one line where Python needs `r = …` + assert to stay under 100 columns; g.remove becomes `-{ }`; the two literal queries stay `s{ }`, the first read with `len(list(r))` because the lazy s{ } value has no __len__ (the RDF line differs from Python's len(r)).
The last query is a bare `s{ }` statement: lazy, never run, as rdflib's own SELECT result is never iterated in the original; unobservable either way (see driver.py).
Symmetry: outside the RDF lines the two files are identical line for line.
header_optimization_notes: The header is `from rdflib import URIRef` and the eight module-level URIRef constants (ldpy: `<urn:...>` terms) that the region reads: all used, nothing to remove. The two files are copies of optimized.py and optimized.ldpy.
